newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Tight money pact powers overnight guilders higher.
newsitem.headline: Tight money pact powers overnight guilders higher.

text.p: Overnight guilder rates surged on Monday but were seen coming down on the back of a string of new government payments into the market on Monday and Tuesday.
Dealers said last week's 2.2 billion guilder special advances allocation had been too tight to tide banks comfortably over the weekend, resulting in a hefty demand for call money.

Call money added more than 10 basis points to trade most of the day at 2.81 percent, even coasting as high as 2.87 percent. Dealers said rates started to slip a little towards the end of the session as social security payments began trickling in.
Trade in other maturities was light to non-existent, dealers said, with most players staying sidelined ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
"A 25-basis point rise in U.S interest rates has largely been factored into the market already," a dealer said.
Three-month guilders were quoted at an unchanged 2.70-percent bid, with one-year money at 2.98-percent bid.
"I have not seen any deals done in these periods today," one dealer said.
The guilder was pegged at 112.11 guilders per 100 marks, the Dutch central bank said.
